figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. (A) The gramicidin S NRPS.17 C: condensation domain; A: adenylation domain; T: thiolation domain; E: epimerization domain; COM:
communication-mediating domain; TE: thioesterase domain. Pentapeptide fPVOL is dimerized and cyclized by the TE-domain. Small case letters
indicate D-amino acids. (B) Top view of C-domain along with its upstream and downstream T-domains. This superimposed model is generated by
aligning the multimodular structure F-A-T-C-A-T from LgrA (PDB: 6MFW)18 and the terminal NRPS module C-A-T-TE from AB3403 (PDB:
4ZXI).19 For simplicity, only the T/C-domain from LgrA (orange/gray) and the T-domain from AB3403 (teal) are shown, and the two Ppant arms
are colored accordingly. The conserved His is shown as a pink sphere.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Identifying specificity-determining residues in the GrsB1-C-domain. (A) The bimodular system used for GrsB1-C mutant screening. The
NRPS module GrsA* selects and activates the original substrate L-Phe and the non-native substrate L-Val. Four DKPs are produced: FP-DKP/fP-
DKP and VP-DKP/vP-DKP, where D-amino acids are indicated in small-case letters. (B) Thirty residues in the GrsB1-C-domain were screened
located in the entry channel (cyan spheres), center region (yellow spheres), and binding site (purple spheres). The flexible latch region and floor
loop are highlighted in green and yellow, respectively. (C) After an initial screening (Figure S6), nine GrsB1 mutants were retested for DKP
formation in purified form. The DKP assay was performed in 1 × DKP assay buffer at 37 °C for 1 h with 1 μM GrsA* and 5 μM GrsB1 variants. As
substrates, 1 mM L-Phe, L-Pro, and L-Val were added. The data were collected from two biological replicates and shown as mean ± SD. The total
DKP yield (nM) is shown as a bar plot in gray, while the Val % and D-form % are indicated as purple and green diamonds, respectively. The mean
of Val % and D-form % of GrsB1 mutants was compared to that of GrsB1 by Dunnett’s test in JMP. The significant differences are highlighted (*: P
≤0.05, **: P ≤0.01, ***: P ≤0.001, ****: P ≤0.0001). (D) Locations of mutational hotspots F155, E386 (binding site: purple), and N256
(entry channel: cyan) and catalytic residue H147 (pink). The Cα-distances to H147 are given in ångströms. The C-domain model is modified from
Figure 1B and labeled with GrsB1 residue numbers and identities. (E) Time courses of DKP formation with GrsB1, GrsB1-F155I, GrsB1-N256A,
and GrsB1-E386L. Reaction rates determined through linear regression are indicated in the bar plot. The data are from two technical replicates and
shown as mean ± SD.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Verifying the mutations in GrsB and other NRPS enzymes. (A) GrsA* and GrsB are able to produce pentapeptides vPVOL, VPVOL, and
fPVOL. (B) The pentapeptide formation of GrsB wildtype and variants in vitro. Pentapeptide formation was performed in 1 × DKP assay buffer,
with 1 mM of L-Phe, L-Pro, L-Val, L-Orn, and L-Leu as substrate, and 0.5 μM of GrsA* and GrsB or its variants. The reaction was incubated at 37 °C
for 3 h. The pentapeptide yield (nM) is shown as a bar plot, while the Val % and D-form % are indicated with diamonds. (C) The pentapeptide
formation of GrsB wildtype and variants in vivo. The total peptide yields are normalized to 100%. (D) DKP formation with GrsA*/TycB1 (left)
and dipeptide formation with GrsA*/SrfAC (right). (E) Sequence logo for position 386 (position number in GrsB1-C) from 2319 DCL and LCL
sequences. The proportion of Glu (E) and Asp (D) is 47.1% in DCL and 12.3% in LCL.
